docstring: A field that states where an artefact's numbers came from must hold a value the emitter resolved, never a path typed into the emitter's own format string. A constant reports the path the author intended to read rather than the path that was read, so it stays correct-looking when the read failed, when the layout moved, and when the artefact is about something else entirely.
pattern: An emitter labels a line or a key as the source of its numbers and fills it from a literal in its own source, so every run of every design publishes the same source claim; when a measured source stamp is later added beside it, the artefact carries two source claims and the constant one can never look wrong.
fix_action: At each write of an artefact, refuse a path-shaped value under a source-naming label when that value is a constant in the emitter rather than a resolved variable, and refuse a second source-naming line in a write that already emits a resolved input list. Render every such line from the resolved values, and record an input that was named but could not be read as unreadable rather than omitting the line, so that an absent input and an unexamined one stay different facts.
measured_before: The published cells' antenna report was 487 bytes byte-identical across two different designs on two different open process kits (sha256 7c614562baacec12...), citing a source path the cell does not contain; the auditor's extractor reported that all four compared artefacts declared nothing.
measured_after: With the subject stamp landed, the same two fixture designs produce different bytes (9020f676... and 2275e38a...) and the JSON source key now holds the resolved log path. The residue is still on origin/main at v1.11.66: the antenna emitter writes the resolved input list and, in the SAME write, a typed sentence naming a fixed log path; a second typed instance sits in another emitter.
fires_on_original: Yes — the original artefact's source key was a typed constant, which is exactly what this rule refuses.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — any emitter whose source-naming field is a literal, including the two that still carry one after the subject-stamp fix landed.
notes: The SUBJECT half of this seam is ALREADY-PROGRAM and landed: the phase-3 runner resolves and stamps the design plus each input with its hash, and two report gates refuse an artefact that names a design the project does not declare. This record is the residue that fix left, not a re-file of it.

design: n/a — one place-and-route run of one digital block
docstring: A report a step offers as sign-off evidence must state which side of place-and-route its numbers come from. The reader that normalises that statement is already correct in treating its absence as undeclared, which means an unstamped report is dropped from the evidence set quietly instead of being refused, and an axis with no evidence reports an incomplete view rather than a failure.
pattern: One report in a family carries the stage statement because its own emitter writes it, and the sibling reports that actually decide the slow and fast corners are written by different emitters that do not, so the rows that matter most are scoped to nothing and the missing evidence is reported as an incomplete view set.
fix_action: Emit the stage statement from one shared helper used by every report emitter in the family rather than per emitter, and add a gate that requires it on every report a step declares as sign-off evidence: missing at emit time is an error, and missing at read time is an undetermined verdict, never a pass.
measured_before: Of three timing reports on one run, the single-corner one carried the stage statement and both multi-corner sign-off reports carried none; 48 of 56 timing rows were then refused by the canonical index as incomplete in scope, and both the setup and the hold axes reported an incomplete view set.
measured_after: Not yet fixed. The lane states the remedy as three added statements in the multi-corner emitters.
fires_on_original: Yes — both unstamped reports are declared sign-off evidence.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — it is keyed on the step's own declaration of what its evidence is, not on these three filenames.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM on the READ side: one module is the single reader of the stage statement and returns undeclared rather than guessing a side. The gap is entirely on the producer side — nothing requires the statement to be written.

design: n/a — one place-and-route run of one digital block
docstring: The stage an artefact claims must be derived from the inputs its own analysis session declared, not from the directory the artefact was filed in. A session that links the pre-layout netlist and loads no extracted parasitics has measured the pre-layout design however its header reads, and the resulting number cannot move when the layout moves.
pattern: A report header states one side of place-and-route while the script beside it links the netlist from the other side and loads no parasitics, so the published number is invariant under every knob that changes the layout and still reads as a measurement of the thing that was built.
fix_action: Parse the emitted analysis script for the netlist it links and for whether it loads extracted parasitics, derive the stage from those declarations, and refuse a header whose claimed basis disagrees with them; a header claiming a post-layout basis in a session that loaded no parasitics is an error, not a note.
measured_before: The shipped power report's own header claimed post-layout numbers; its session linked a netlist carrying 287 standard-cell instances and read no parasitics, while the routed netlist carries 3373. Same tool, same library, same constraints, same activity basis: 0.306 mW shipped against 0.573 mW post-route, understating total power by 46.6 per cent, with the clock group reported as exactly zero against 33.7 per cent of real power.
measured_after: Not fixed in the flow. The lane's extractor works around it by deriving the stage from the session's declared inputs instead of from the directory, which is this rule applied by one consumer rather than enforced at the producer.
fires_on_original: Yes — the header and the session inputs disagree in the shipped artefact.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — the comparison is between a claimed basis and declared inputs, both of which every analysis session has.
notes: A zero for a whole power group is the clearest instance of the general failure: an absent contributor read as a measured zero.

design: n/a — one place-and-route run of one digital block
docstring: A path an emitter writes into a generated analysis script must be relative to the project root or to a declared tool root. An absolute run-directory path makes two runs of one configuration hash differently, so any identity taken over that script identifies where the run happened instead of what was configured, and the two runs can never be compared as the same measurement.
pattern: A generator writes the absolute path of the directory a run happened in into the script that defines the measurement, so the artefact that ought to be the stable identity of a configuration becomes unique per run and every identity check over it either refuses or is dropped.
fix_action: Write every path in a generated analysis script relative to the project root or to a declared tool root, and fail the emit when an absolute path outside those roots is written. Extend the existing absolute-path rule from shipped source and from analog decks to the population of generated analysis scripts; do not solve it by dropping the script from the identity.
measured_before: The emitted power analysis script linked the netlist by an absolute path under the run's own trial directory, so the run identity check refused it and the lane excluded the script from the identity and said so.
measured_after: Not fixed; the exclusion is a disclosure, not a repair.
fires_on_original: Yes — the absolute run path is in the emitted script.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — the rule is about the shape of a written path, not about this script.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for two other populations: one gate refuses a personal or absolute home path in shipped plugin source, and another refuses a non-standard absolute include path in an analog deck. Neither covers a generated digital analysis script, which is the population that defeated the identity here.

design: n/a — one place-and-route run of one digital block
docstring: A key a floor check proves an axis from must be a key that some producer emits. When the consumer's name and the producer's name for one quantity differ, the check reports the value as not measured on every view of every run, which reads as missing evidence about that run instead of as a wiring fault that no run can ever satisfy.
pattern: A consumer proves an axis from one metric name while the extractor publishes the same quantity under another, so the axis is unprovable on every run and each run appears to blame its own evidence rather than the wiring.
fix_action: Cross-reference the key names consumers prove from against the key names producers emit, and error at wiring time on any required key that no producer emits, naming both sides. Model it on the existing gate that requires a producer for every document field a checker reads: same shape, different population.
measured_before: The hold axis proves from one slack name; the extractor emits the quantity the reports actually print under a different name. Across all six timing artefacts of a baseline run the required key was not measured on every view, with the reason that the artefact carries no such line. The axis is structurally unprovable from this flow's evidence.
fires_on_original: Yes — the required key has no producer anywhere in the flow.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — the same comparison over any other axis, which is how the five other undetermined axes on the same run should be triaged.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for document fields: a blocking gate already refuses a new reader of a field no document populates, and its docstring records five separate measurements of that same shape. Metric keys are the population it does not cover.

design: n/a — one place-and-route run of one digital block
docstring: An artefact whose own verdict field declares it a measurement rather than a sign-off may not be read as the evidence for a floor check. A reader that derives a count from it gets either an unmeasured row or, worse, a zero — and a zero here is a clean result that nobody computed, against a limit that was never named.
pattern: A consumer resolves an axis to the emitter's raw measurement file instead of to the sign-off checker that compares that measurement against a declared limit, so the absence of a count becomes indistinguishable from a count of zero and the axis reports a pass that no comparison produced.
fix_action: Refuse an artefact that declares itself a measurement as evidence for a floor check; resolve the sign-off producer registered for that axis instead, and where no sign-off ran, report that it did not run together with the reason. Never substitute zero for a count that was not computed.
measured_before: The electromigration artefact carries a count of analysed segments and a maximum segment current and no violation count and no declared limit; the axis reading it resolved to not measured with that reason. The emitter's own comment states the artefact is not a sign-off verdict and that the comparison is decided downstream.
measured_after: Not fixed on the consumer side.
fires_on_original: Yes — the consumed artefact carries the declaration that makes it refusable.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — the same declaration is used by the sibling voltage-drop artefact and by any future measurement emitter that adopts it.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM on the producer side: a program exists that performs the real per-segment current-density comparison against the limit read from the process kit's own technology file, and reports offenders. The count the axis wanted is computed by that program; the consumer read the wrong artefact.

design: n/a — the flow's own sign-off report path
docstring: A path one step declares as its own required output may be written only by that step's producer. A helper that runs the same checker with fewer arguments leaves a strictly weaker verdict wearing the declared filename, and a release-gating tier then grades the weaker file without any indication that a stronger one existed.
pattern: A precheck delegates to the same checker with a reduced argument set and writes the result at the flow's canonical evidence path, so one path has two writers and the writer that dropped the sign-off scoping wins by running last.
fix_action: Refuse any write to a path that the flow declares as another step's required output. A non-declaring writer must use both a private directory and a different basename, because discovery here is by recursive glob and a private directory alone is still found. Guard the rule with a negative control asserting the historical paths are still recognised as flow-owned, so the check cannot pass over an empty set.
measured_before: Run at one path, the declaring step's argument form produced 811 bytes with two findings and the scoping key populated; the delegate's reduced form produced 308 bytes with one finding and no scope keys at all. Four of the five delegates wrote into flow-canonical report paths and three of those are declared required outputs.
measured_after: Fixed on an unpushed branch by giving the delegates a private directory AND different basenames, with a guard test reading the live flow definition plus the negative control. The rule is NOT in this repository: the branch could not be pushed.
fires_on_original: Yes — the delegate write is exactly what it refuses.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — it is keyed on the flow's own output declarations, so it covers the other four delegate paths and any future helper that reuses a canonical path.
notes: The same lane measured that fixing the clobber ALONE would have turned the failing cell green while leaving the real gap invisible, because the accidental consumer disappears with it. The declaration and the guard have to land together.

design: n/a — repository gates run against a fixture tree
docstring: A pointer read from the environment may replace a location that is absent; it may never replace one the caller named on the command line. A program that lets the pointer win measures a tree the caller did not ask about and publishes the verdict under the caller's name, and the louder the pointer's tree, the more convincing the wrong answer looks.
pattern: A checker resolves its subject from an environment pointer after parsing an explicit location argument and lets the pointer win unconditionally, so a caller who names a small fixture is answered about a large shared tree, the fixture's own defect is never seen, and binding the shared tree and testing against fixtures become mutually exclusive.
fix_action: Route every consumer through the one resolver that already states the rule — the pointer applies only when the named location is not a directory — and announce in the output both which location was scanned and which pointer was set and not followed. Add a source scan that refuses a pointer read which overwrites an already-parsed location argument.
measured_before: Reproduced by me on origin/main at v1.11.66: three sites still spell it as an unconditional override — an evidence-structure checker overwriting its tree argument, and two pointer checkers preferring the environment over their root argument. In the lane's measurement a checker given an explicit two-path subject instead reported a pass over 8309 tracked paths of the shared tree.
measured_after: On the lane's branch, 21 of 23 named failures close, 0 new, 0 regressions across a 32-file sweep; every shipped call shape still reaches the pointer and says so. The branch is pushed and NOT landed — the three sites above are the current state of the default branch.
fires_on_original: Yes — all three sites match the shape.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — it is a source-level shape, so it catches the fourth consumer written next week.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM: the resolver holds the correct rule and its docstring states it in as many words. Nothing forced the three consumers through it, which is why a correct rule sat beside three copies of the wrong one.

docstring: An aggregate of test results records the tree it measured but not the runtime it ran in, so a failure caused by a dependency the runtime cannot import is charged to the tree. Two aggregates produced by different runtimes are then differenced as if they were one measurement, and the difference is read as a change in the code.
pattern: A selection asks the runtime to load a plugin the runtime does not carry, every test in those files dies at load rather than at assertion, and the resulting failures are counted against the revision under test because nothing in the record names the runtime that produced them.
fix_action: Stamp the aggregate with the runtime's identity — the image reference actually executed, the interpreter version, and the set of plugins the selection requests that the runtime cannot import — and refuse to difference two aggregates whose runtime stamps differ, naming the difference instead of subtracting across it.
measured_before: Of 127 failures in one tier arm, 28 were one missing test plugin and 26 of those disappeared on a second runtime; separating them from the 51 that are real about the tree took five controlled arms differing only in runtime, pointer binding, instrumentation and revision.
measured_after: Not fixed; the attribution exists only in that lane's write-up.
fires_on_original: Yes — the aggregate carried no runtime identity, which is what made the five arms necessary.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — any dependency the runtime lacks, and any comparison of two arms run in different places.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for the flow's own container: a program records and can enforce which image a run actually executed, for exactly this reason. The test aggregate is the population it does not cover.

docstring: A checkout prepared for a gate run must state which revision it holds and prove it against the upstream reference it names. A clone taken from a local repository inherits that repository's own branch position, which can be many releases behind, so the run measures a revision nobody asked for and reports it under the newer one's name.
pattern: Automation prepares a checkout by cloning a branch name from a local path, the local branch position is stale, the commit under test is absent from the resulting tree, and the gate run produces a complete and internally consistent verdict about the wrong revision.
fix_action: Resolve the named upstream reference from the upstream remote at preparation time and refuse when the prepared checkout's head differs, printing both. When the upstream cannot be reached, report that the revision could not be confirmed rather than passing — a checkout that cannot prove its revision is undetermined, not correct.
measured_before: A clone made this way landed on a branch position many releases old and did not contain the commit under test at all; the run had to be re-pointed at the upstream and reset before it measured anything about the intended revision.
measured_after: Not fixed. The existing preflight proves a different property.
fires_on_original: Yes — the stale clone's head differs from the upstream reference it was asked for.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — any prepared checkout, including ones cut from a shared multi-branch working area.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for self-containment: a landed preflight refuses a checkout that borrows its objects from another repository and states that it is self-contained. It says nothing about WHICH revision the self-contained checkout holds, and those are different facts.

docstring: A checkout cloned from a local path shares object storage with the source repository unless the clone is told not to. A preflight that requires a self-contained checkout then refuses the very checkout the automation prepared, every time, and the refusal names the checkout rather than the preparation that made it that way.
pattern: One part of a system prepares a checkout with default options while another part requires that checkouts be self-contained, so the requirement and the preparation contradict each other permanently and the failure is read as a property of the subject instead of the setup.
fix_action: Scan the source for any clone of a local path that does not disable hardlinked and shared object storage, and require the option at every checkout-preparation site. Pair it with the preflight so the two cannot drift: the option the preflight demands is the option the preparation passes.
measured_before: Reproduced by me on origin/main at v1.11.66: the option appears nowhere in this repository's own source or scripts — zero occurrences. Two independent lanes hit the refusal and escaped it only by passing the option by hand.
fires_on_original: Yes — the preparation site has no such option.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — it is a source-level shape over every clone of a local path.
notes: Smallest record in this set, and the cheapest: a preflight that refuses a state nothing in the repository is able to avoid is a guaranteed false alarm rather than a gate.

design: n/a — a refusal message printed by a preflight
docstring: A refusal that prints a command must render that command from the same argument list a caller would run, and a test must execute it. A remedy assembled as prose beside the code that runs the real thing drifts from it silently, and the reader who follows the printed line exactly is the one who discovers the drift.
pattern: A refusal prints an invocation that omits an argument the entry point requires, so following the printed remedy exactly fails without ever running the command, and the reader concludes the refusal itself is wrong rather than that the message is stale.
fix_action: Build the printed remedy from one argument-list builder shared with the caller that runs it, so the printed line and the executed line cannot drift. Execute it in a test that asserts BOTH a zero exit and a marker in the output — a zero exit alone is the signature of an entry point that swallowed the command — and add the negative control that the same list without the entry-point argument fails, otherwise the test passes against an image with no entry point at all.
measured_before: Run verbatim, the printed remedy returned an unexpected-option error and exit 1, with the command never executed. With the entry point's own leading argument added it ran and returned the marker, in 0.58 seconds against the local image.
measured_after: Fixed on a pushed but unlanded branch: one builder, four tests, two of which execute the remedy and one of which is the negative control. Not present on the default branch.
fires_on_original: Yes — the printed line and the working line differ by one leading argument.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — any refusal, error or documentation line in the tree that prints a command it does not itself build.
notes: One correction to the record it came from: the verbatim remedy is not silent — it exits non-zero. It still does not run.

design: n/a — a design declaring its constraints as derivations
docstring: A generator that falls back to a built-in value when it cannot read one from the design must say which of the two happened, and cite the input it read. Without that line a default and a design-declared value are the same bytes, so nobody can see that the design's own statement was never applied, and every verdict downstream is about a constraint the design may never have asked for.
pattern: A generator emits a value that could have come either from the design's own input documents or from its own last-resort default, marks neither, and the resulting artefact is indistinguishable in both cases, so a silently unread input produces a complete and plausible run about the wrong constraint.
fix_action: For every value a generator can either read or default, emit a disclosure line beside it stating which happened; for a read value name the input file and line it came from and the key that matched. A design that declares nothing keeps the historical default byte-for-byte and its disclosure says exactly that, and two input rows that match with different values are refused rather than resolved by list order.
measured_before: A design stated its clock period in a table keyed by standard-cell library and its input delay as a percentage of that period. Neither was read: the run signed off at the generator's defaults, a period of 20 against a declared 24 — a 20 per cent over-constraint — and a fixed input delay of 2 against a declared 4.8, an under-constraint of 2.8 in the opposite direction. Both are the same class: a declared RELATIONSHIP read as if it were a declared VALUE, or not read at all.
measured_after: Three full runs on one design, same image and host: the applied period moved from 20 to 24 and the input delay from 2 to 4.8, and the design still met timing. Of the table's six rows against the old default, five make sign-off STRICTER, so the rule is not a relaxation.
fires_on_original: Yes — the emitted constraint file carried both values with no disclosure of where either came from.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — it is keyed on the existence of a fallback default, not on these two values, so it covers every other generator value that can be read or defaulted.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for these two values specifically: a program landed at v1.11.5 that reads the period from a table keyed by cell library and computes the input delay as the declared fraction, and writes a disclosure naming the matched key and the document line. What did NOT land is the general rule that every read-or-defaulted value must be marked; that program marks two.

design: n/a — routing of one digital block
title: A fatal condition downgraded to a warning leaves no machine-readable statement that the stage did not complete
problem: The forked place-and-route tool's standing practice is to downgrade a fatal abort to a warning so that a later change order can still proceed. The downgraded condition then survives only as a change of severity in the log: there is no stable, machine-readable statement that the stage did not complete and no identifier a reader can rely on across versions. A downstream reader screening for error-severity lines therefore stops seeing the condition at the exact moment it is downgraded, and each further downgrade removes another condition from the screen by construction.
golden_sample: none — no build of this tool emits the completion statement this record asks for, so the golden sample has to be created by the enhancement rather than captured from an existing run.
bad_sample: the routing log of a place-and-route run in which a pin the router could not reach is reported only as a downgraded warning, which the plugin has to scan for separately because it is no longer an error-severity line.
tool_enhancement: In the fork's router and resizer, every condition that has been downgraded from fatal must also emit a stable machine-readable completion record naming the stage, whether that stage finished, and which condition prevented it — independent of the severity the message was downgraded to. A reader must be able to ask whether the stage completed without enumerating the tool's current identifiers, so that a future downgrade adds to what the reader sees instead of subtracting from it.
pattern: A tool converts a fatal condition into a warning so that a flow can continue past it, and each such downgrade silently removes that condition from the set a downstream severity screen can see, so the screen weakens with every release while continuing to report a clean result on the runs it can no longer judge.
why_not_bucket_a: A plugin-side rule can only enumerate the identifiers the fork has ALREADY downgraded — which is what it does today, with a list of error markers plus a separately added scan for the one identifier most recently downgraded to a warning. That list can never include the next downgrade, because the downgrade exists precisely to stop the tool from erroring, so a downstream rule is guaranteed to be one release behind and to fail in the passing direction. The completion statement has to come from the tool that knows it did not complete.
suggested_fix: Add a completion record to the fork's routing and resizing stages that is emitted regardless of severity downgrades, and make the plugin read that record instead of screening the log for error-severity identifiers.
component: forked place-and-route tool, routing and resizing stages
session_context: Captured while auditing which produced artefacts carry the identity of what they measured; a routing stage that aborted and a routing stage that finished currently produce reports the reader cannot separate once the abort has been downgraded.
measured_before: The plugin's own emitter carries a list of error-severity markers used to decide that routing did not complete, plus a separately maintained scan for one identifier the fork downgraded from fatal to a warning so that a post-route change order can continue; the code's own comment records that each downgrade moves a condition out of the set the gate can see, by construction.
fires_on_original: Yes — the downgraded identifier is the reason the separate warning scan had to be written.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — every other condition the fork has downgraded or will downgrade under the same practice.

design: n/a — the flow's own output declarations
title: An artefact index that matches whole-path literals cannot tell a reader from a writer, nor see a reader that resolves the path at run time
pattern: An index that maps an artefact to the programs whose source contains its full path cannot see a consumer that reaches the same artefact by basename or by recursive glob, and cannot separate a reader from a writer, so an artefact with several real readers is recorded as having none, and removing one accidental mention makes the gap look closed.
why_not_bucket_a: A deterministic rule is the right answer and the input is a program's source text; what a program cannot decide from a bare basename occurrence is whether that occurrence is a read, a write, or a name in a mapping table or a comment. The measured population is eight undeclared step-designated outputs mentioned by basename elsewhere, and several of those mentions are not reads — so the widened pattern shipped as-is produces false findings, which this module's own doctrine treats as a defect to kill rather than a cost to accept. Deciding it needs source-level data-flow analysis plus an individual verdict on each of the eight, which is a new program and a fixture corpus, not a wider regular expression.
suggested_fix: Build a read-versus-write aware source analyser for artefact paths that resolves basename and glob access, triage the eight measured occurrences individually before turning it on, and keep the current limit asserted by a test so that widening the index fails loudly instead of quietly outdating the comment that records the limit.
session_context: Found while establishing whether a sign-off artefact read by three programs and declared by none was a real gap; the index that was supposed to answer that question named a writer as a reader and missed all three real readers.
measured_before: The index charged the right path and named the wrong consumer: the program it named does not read the artefact, it runs the checker that writes it. The three real readers reach it by basename or recursive glob and were invisible — one of them grades a release tier on it and reports not-run when it is absent, one echoes its verdict into the sign-off summary, and one reads two of its keys. Removing the accidental mention alone turned the failing cell green with all three real readers untouched.
measured_after: Not attempted. The limit is written into a test instead, so widening the index goes red rather than quiet.
fires_on_original: Yes — the original artefact is one of the eight.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — the other seven were measured and listed by the same sweep.

title: A published run carries the reports it produced but not the inputs those reports name
pattern: A published run carries its reports but not the inputs those reports were measured from, so a later reader can neither re-derive a number nor re-measure the run under a rule that did not exist when it was published, and the resulting gap reads as history rather than as missing evidence.
why_not_bucket_a: The check itself IS deterministic and belongs in Bucket A — a published run either carries the inputs its own reports name or it does not, and that is a file-existence test over paths the reports themselves state. What is large is everything the check needs before it can be turned on: the contract for which inputs a published run must carry has to be written, every already-published run has to be measured against it, and runs have to be re-published from a flow carrying the identity stamps, because switching the check on today fails the entire corpus for a reason that predates the rule.
suggested_fix: Write the publication contract for which inputs a published run must carry beside its reports, measure the existing corpus against it and record the shortfall per run, then enable the check for newly published runs only and close the historical entries as each run is re-published rather than by widening an exemption.
component: published evidence corpus and its publication contract
session_context: Two recorded adversarial findings about unattributable sign-off reports could not be closed even after the mechanism that fixes them landed, because the published runs they cite carry no inputs to re-measure from.
measured_before: The published run carries none of the place-and-route working directory, so its reports cannot be regenerated from it; the two recorded findings therefore still read as succeeding attacks with the defence in place, and the record was deliberately NOT regenerated, on the grounds that closing them would record a publication schedule as security progress.
measured_after: Not fixed; what is needed is a published run made with the identity stamps, which is the acceptance test the originating lane could not run.
fires_on_original: Yes — the two runs compared in the original finding both fail it.
fires_on_a_different_instance: Yes — it is keyed on what a run's own reports name as their inputs, so it applies to every published run.

design: n/a — four numbers cited in a work order
why_discard: The four failing numbers this work started from could not be located: every checkout on the host was searched for them, and every comparable run there reports the opposite verdict. With no artefact of the run that produced them reachable, the class of the defect is unknown, so there is nothing measured to generalise from and a record would capture a hypothesis in the shape of a finding. The generalisable half of the same episode IS captured, as separate records: a reported measurement that does not name the runtime and the revision that produced it cannot be attributed, and that is a rule about the record, not about these four numbers. Discarding this is not a claim that the numbers were wrong — only that nothing about them was measurable from here, and the lane manufactured no violation to fix in their place.
